paper_metadata.title: Solving Quantitative Reasoning Problems with Language Models
paper_metadata.abstract: Language models have achieved remarkable performance on a wide range of tasks that require natural language understanding. Nevertheless, state-of-the-art models have generally struggled with tasks that require quantitative reasoning, such as solving mathematics, science, and engineering problems at the college level. To help close this gap, we introduce Minerva, a large language model pretrained on general natural language data and further trained on technical content. The model achieves state-of-the-art performance on technical benchmarks without the use of external tools. We also evaluate our model on over two hundred undergraduate-level problems in physics, biology, chemistry, economics, and other sciences that require quantitative reasoning, and find that the model can correctly answer nearly a third of them.

extraction_data.innovation: Data juxtaposition: Training on a large dataset that pairs natural language with formal mathematical language (equations, diagrams) collected from arXiv and processed webpages, improving mathematical reasoning over prior models; Chain-of-thought reasoning: Prompting the model to output step-by-step solutions in a chain-of-thought context, enabling it to solve unseen problems without explicit training on evaluation datasets; Majority voting: Sampling multiple solutions per problem and filtering/voting to select the final answer, significantly improving performance over greedy decoding without requiring external tools or verifiers.
extraction_data.pretraining_corpus: arXiv preprints, webpages processed to minimize loss of mathematical content, MIT OpenCourseWare (OCW)
extraction_data.finetuning_task: Supervised fine-tuning on math and science datasets, Continued pre-training on mathematical dataset, Supervised fine-tuning on mathematical reasoning
extraction_data.extension: Continued pre-training (finetuning) on a specialized mathematical dataset.
